questions.prompt: Put the stages of water treatment in the correct order.
questions.explain: Largest things out first, germs last: screening → sedimentation → filtration → disinfection.

questions.prompt: Match each stage to what it removes.
questions.explain: Each stage targets smaller and smaller impurities.

questions.prompt: Why is alum (phitkari) added to muddy water?
options: To make tiny mud particles clump together and settle faster
To make the water taste better
questions.explain: This is called loading: alum makes fine particles stick together into heavier clumps that sink.

options: Germs can hide in dirt, so disinfection works best on clear water
It doesn't matter when it's done
questions.explain: Suspended particles shield germs and use up chlorine, so solids are removed first.

questions.prompt: Water is clear after filtering through sand. Is it safe to drink?
options: Not yet: germs and dissolved substances may still be in it
Yes, if it's in a clean bottle
questions.explain: Filtering removes particles, not most germs or dissolved substances. It still needs disinfection.

questions.prompt: Which methods kill germs in drinking water? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: Boiling, chlorine and UV light kill germs. Sedimentation only lets solids settle.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to make muddy water safe to drink at home.
steps: Let the water stand so mud settles (sedimentation)
Filter it through a clean cloth or filter
Boil it for a few minutes and let it cool

questions.prompt: Why don't big cities use distillation to clean all their tap water?
options: Boiling millions of litres every day would need enormous amounts of energy and money
questions.explain: Distillation works but is very energy-hungry at a city scale. Screening, sedimentation, filtration and chlorination are far cheaper.

questions.text: Water that is safe to drink is called ___ water.
questions.explain: Potable water is safe for drinking.

questions.prompt: RO water purifiers remove dissolved salts but waste 2–3 litres of water for every litre they clean. Suggest TWO ways a family could reduce this waste, and say why it matters in a city like Bengaluru.
questions.modelAnswer: 1) Collect the RO waste water and reuse it for mopping floors, flushing toilets or washing vehicles. 2) Only use RO if the water really has high dissolved salts; otherwise a UV or candle filter plus boiling may be enough. It matters because Bengaluru often faces water shortages in summer and depends on water pumped from far away and on groundwater.
rubric: I gave one practical way to reuse or reduce RO waste
I gave a second, different way
I linked it to water shortage / sustainability in Bengaluru
